text:
alice: Quick question — probe scheduling + benchmark stitching for new model intake. bench says p50 45ms but runtime p95 spikes to 300ms for short prompts. anyone seen similar?
ben: yep. usually first suspect is KV cache warmup + batching not matching bench traces. are bench runs replaying real prefix distributions?
carla: not always. our bench harness uses stratified prompts but often omits small-hot-cache cases. i think we need explicit probe windows that capture 'cold', 'warm', and 'hot' states.
eva: +1. also need the probe to exercise tail-case IO (disk swap, quantized kernel paths). otherwise the benchmark is optimistic.
alice: thinking of adding a "stitch" step that takes bench microtraces and assigns probe schedules for runtime canaries. suggestions on interface? lightweight vs. stateful prober?
ben: interface idea: prober -> report {trace_id, sequence_len, cache_state, cpu_mem, kernel_path} as one-line JSONL. then a stitcher service maps traces to canary schedules. cheap and auditable.
carla: sgtm. keep prober stateless to avoid long-lived agents. we can store small TTL metadata in redis for correlation.
frank: tradeoff: stateless prober -> easier to scale, but stitching becomes more complex. If probe frequency is too high we overload dedicated pools. need cooldown windows per-model.
alice: agreed. proposal sketch:
```yaml
prober:
  interval: 5m
  burst: 3
  cooldown: 15m
  sampling_policy: "stratified:short,mid,long; weight:[0.5,0.3,0.2]"
stitcher:
  target_canary_pct: 0.1
  map_rules:
    - when: cache_state == cold -> prefer low-latency nodes
    - when: cache_state == hot -> sample across dedicated p50 slots
```
ben: i'd add a "prefetch_consistency" flag to make sure bench replays can pre-prime caches when desired. otherwise we can't reproduce warm-paths.
eva: metrics to capture for each probe: token_throughput, p50/p95/99, kv_hits, small_allocs, kernel_variant. add tags for quantization level.
carla: also capture "probe_reason" tag (golden-input, smoke, regression-check). helps filtering in console and alerts.
frank: question about gating: do we fail admission if runtime canary diverges > 2x p95 from bench? or just flag?
alice: i'd prefer a tiered failure: >2x p95 -> block on-prem/adopt canary-only, >3x -> block. we should codify thresholds per-model-class.
ben: agreed. thresholds should be model-profiled: small-context chat vs long-form generation. store thresholds in registry.
devops-bot: scheduled job created: `prober/eng-ml/1762345678-stitch` runs every 5m. next run: 2026-02-12T15:02:00Z :robot_face:
eva: nice — can the job emit a sample payload link? makes triage faster.
devops-bot: link: https://ci.redwood/probes/1762345678/sample-20260212.jsonl
carla: one more nit — kv cache priming on dedicated pools can mask cold-starts. maybe probes should include an explicit `reset_kv: true|false` flag so we can measure cold.
ben: yeah, and add `backend_hint` so stitcher can route to dedicated vs shared runtime.
frank: operationally, we also need a circuit-breaker that reduces probe rate if latency > SLO and error >= 1% for 5m. avoid causing incidents.
alice: i'll draft an RFC for the prober/stitcher interface + sample JSON schema and thresholds table. planning to sync Weds.
eva: thanks — can you include a sample alerting runbook? those thresholds are sensitive.
alice: will do. thx all :thumbsup:
